newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-STATE COMMERCIAL BANK'S 1996 LOSSES HUGE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-STATE COMMERCIAL BANK'S 1996 LOSSES HUGE.

text.p: Lithuania's finance ministry said on Thursday that the troubled State Commercial Bank lost 172.9 million litas in 1996.
The ministry also said in a statement that the losses largely stemmed from provisions needed to cover bad loans from 1992 to 1995.
The ministry added that the bank's liabilities exceeded its assets at the end of 1996 by 43.7 million litas.
It said that the bank's expenses in 1996 reached 242.9 million litas.
"Despite these difficulties, during the first quarter of 1997 the bank had a profit of 347,000 litas," the ministry said.
The finance ministry added that it had sent out invitations to a number of Lithuanian and foreign banks, asking them if they were interested in participating in the privatisation of the bank.
It said it expected responses before next Monday.

Seeking to avert a fresh crisis in the banking sector last year, the government injected 165 million litas in fresh capital into the bank after it emerged that it was crippled by a staggering bad loan portfolio.
